stem: A project has four activities. A takes 3 days and starts the job. B takes 4 days and C takes 6 days; both follow A. D takes 2 days and follows both B and C. What is the total float of activity B?
eli5: In the critical path method the longest path through the network sets the project duration, and activities on it have zero float. Total float is the time an activity can slip without delaying the project: late start minus early start.
solution:
Path A-B-D = 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 days. Path A-C-D = 3 + 6 + 2 = 11 days, which is critical.

B and C run in parallel between the same events, so B can slip by the difference: total float of B = 6 - 4 = 2 days.

stem: At a status date a project has a planned value of $100,000, an earned value of $90,000 and an actual cost of $95,000. What is the cost performance index?
eli5: Earned value management compares the budgeted value of work done (EV) with what it cost (AC) and with what was scheduled (PV). CPI = EV / AC; below 1.0 means over budget. SPI = EV / PV; below 1.0 means behind schedule.

stem: An excavator has a 1.5 m^{3} bucket and a cycle time of 30 s. It works 50 minutes of each hour. What is its hourly production?
eli5: Equipment production = volume per cycle × cycles per hour × efficiency. The efficiency factor (working minutes per 60) accounts for delays, operator breaks and repositioning.
solution:
Cycles per hour = 3,600 / 30 = 120.

Ideal production = 1.5 × 120 = 180 m^{3}/h.

Efficiency = 50 / 60 = 0.833.

Production = 180 × 0.833 = 150 m^{3}/h.

stem: Put these milestones of a design-bid-build contract in order, from first (top) to last (bottom).
eli5: The owner asks for prices, opens them, picks a builder, tells the builder to start, takes over the nearly finished job, then pays the last of the money.
solution: The owner advertises for bids, then opens them on the stated date. The notice of award names the winner. The notice to proceed starts the contract time. Substantial completion is when the owner can use the work. Final payment closes the contract.

solution: The work is first inspected for substantial completion. Remaining items go on a punch list, the contractor completes them, a final inspection confirms it, and only then is final payment made and retainage released.

stem: Put the steps of critical path scheduling in order, from first (top) to last (bottom).

items.text: Forward pass: earliest start and finish dates
Calculate float and mark the critical path
Set which activities depend on which
Backward pass: latest start and finish dates

eli5: The owner asks for prices, opens them, picks a builder, tells the builder to start, takes over the nearly finished job, then pays the last of the money.
solution:
Activities and their dependencies come first, because they define the network. Durations are then estimated.

The forward pass works from the start to give the earliest dates; the backward pass works from the finish to give the latest dates. Float, late minus early, comes last, and the activities with zero float form the critical path.
terms: critical path
the longest chain of dependent activities through a schedule; it sets the project duration
float

stem: On a grading plan, what do closely spaced contour lines indicate?
eli5: Contour lines join points of equal elevation. Close spacing means steep ground and wide spacing means flat ground. Closed loops normally mark a hill; hachures on the downhill side mark a depression. Contours bend upstream where they cross a valley.
solution:
Contours join points of equal elevation at a fixed vertical interval.

The closer they are in plan, the less horizontal distance per interval, so the steeper the slope.

stem: On a topographic map, a set of closed contour lines carries short tick marks (hachures) pointing inward. What does this show?
eli5: Contour lines join points of equal elevation. Close spacing means steep ground and wide spacing means flat ground. Closed loops normally mark a hill; hachures on the downhill side mark a depression. Contours bend upstream where they cross a valley.
solution: Closed contours with inward hachures mean the ground falls toward the centre, which is a depression. Without hachures the same loops would be a hill.

stem: On a contour map, the contour lines across a site are evenly spaced and far apart. What does this indicate?
eli5: Contour lines join points of equal elevation. Close spacing means steep ground and wide spacing means flat ground. Closed loops normally mark a hill; hachures on the downhill side mark a depression. Contours bend upstream where they cross a valley.
solution: Each contour is a line of equal elevation, so the ground rises by one contour interval between neighbours. Lines far apart mean a long run for that rise, a gentle slope; even spacing means the slope is uniform.

stem: Under which project delivery method does the owner hold a single contract with one entity for both design and construction?
eli5: Delivery methods differ in who holds which contract. Design-bid-build: separate, sequential contracts for design and construction. Design-build: one contract for both. Construction manager at risk: a manager joins during design and guarantees a maximum price.
solution:
In design-build the owner contracts with one entity that designs and builds.

In design-bid-build the owner holds separate contracts with a designer and a contractor.

stem: An owner hires a designer under one contract and, once the design is complete, awards a separate construction contract to the lowest responsive bidder. Which delivery method is this?
eli5: Delivery methods differ in who holds which contract. Design-bid-build: separate, sequential contracts for design and construction. Design-build: one contract for both. Construction manager at risk: a manager joins during design and guarantees a maximum price.
solution:
Two separate contracts, with construction bid after the design is finished, is design-bid-build, the traditional method.

Design-build would put design and construction under a single contract.

stem: Under which delivery method does the owner first hire a designer to complete the plans, then award a separate construction contract by competitive bid?

stem: Which bond guarantees that a contractor will pay its subcontractors and suppliers?
eli5: A surety bond is a three-party guarantee from a surety to the owner. A bid bond guarantees that the bidder will sign the contract at its bid price. A performance bond guarantees completion of the work. A payment bond guarantees that subcontractors and suppliers are paid.
solution:
A payment bond protects subcontractors and suppliers.

A bid bond guarantees the bidder will sign the contract, and a performance bond guarantees the work will be completed.

stem: Which bond guarantees that the contractor will complete the work in accordance with the contract?
eli5: A surety bond is a three-party guarantee from a surety to the owner. A bid bond guarantees that the bidder will sign the contract at its bid price. A performance bond guarantees completion of the work. A payment bond guarantees that subcontractors and suppliers are paid.
solution: Completion of the work is what a performance bond guarantees. If the contractor defaults, the surety arranges or pays for completion up to the bond amount.
needs: Ethics and Professional Practice: Contracts and contract law

stem: Which bond protects the owner if the low bidder refuses to sign the contract at its bid price?
eli5: A surety bond is a three-party guarantee from a surety to the owner. A bid bond guarantees that the bidder will sign the contract at its bid price. A performance bond guarantees completion of the work. A payment bond guarantees that subcontractors and suppliers are paid.
solution:
A bid bond guarantees that the bidder will enter into the contract at the price bid. If it does not, the surety pays the owner the difference up to the bond amount.

A performance bond covers completion of the work; a payment bond covers subcontractors and suppliers.

verify.basis: Standard definitions of construction surety bonds

stem: A project has a planned value of $100,000 and an earned value of $90,000 at the status date. What is the schedule variance?
eli5: Earned value analysis measures progress in budget terms. Schedule variance is SV = EV - PV and cost variance is CV = EV - AC. A positive variance is favourable: ahead of schedule or under budget.
solution: SV = EV - PV = 90,000 - 100,000 = -$10,000, so the project is behind schedule.
terms: earned value
the budgeted cost of the work actually completed to date

stem: A project has a planned value of $150,000, an earned value of $180,000 and an actual cost of $170,000 at the status date. What is the schedule variance?
eli5: Earned value analysis measures progress in budget terms. Schedule variance is SV = EV - PV and cost variance is CV = EV - AC. A positive variance is favourable: ahead of schedule or under budget.
solution:
SV = EV - PV = 180,000 - 150,000 = $30,000. The project has earned more than was planned by this date, so it is ahead of schedule.

For reference, CV = EV - AC = 180,000 - 170,000 = $10,000, under budget.
terms: earned value
the budgeted cost of the work actually completed to date

stem: A project has a planned value of $240,000 and an earned value of $255,000 at the status date. What is the schedule variance?

A positive value means more work has been completed than was planned by this date: the project is ahead of schedule.

stem: A crew places 40 m^{2} of formwork per day. There are 1,200 m^{2} to place and 2 crews working. How many working days are needed?
eli5: Activity duration = quantity of work / (crew productivity × number of crews). Durations found this way feed the schedule network.
solution:
Daily output = 2 × 40 = 80 m^{2}/day.

Duration = \frac{1,200}{80} = 15 working days.

stem: Fresh concrete with a unit weight of 24.0 kN/m^{3} is placed quickly to a height of 3.0 m in a wall form. Treating it as a liquid, what is the maximum pressure on the form?
eli5: Until it begins to set, fresh concrete behaves like a heavy liquid, so form pressure rises linearly with depth to unit weight × height at the bottom. Slower placing lets the lower concrete stiffen and caps the pressure.
solution: Maximum pressure = 24.0 × 3.0 = 72.0 kPa at the base of the form.
